lines.text: Luis stepped into a slushy puddle at mile two.
By lunch, his toes were numb.
Wet socks pull heat out of your feet fast.
Here's the fix. Carry a dry spare pair of wool socks in a sealed bag.
At the break, dry your feet and pull on the spare pair.
Wool still keeps you warmer than cotton when it gets damp.
He hiked out with warm toes.
Save this before your next cold hike.
